newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia tells funds not to worry about dam.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia tells funds not to worry about dam.

text.p: Malaysia's Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim has assured fund managers there will be ample liquidity to sustain the country's largest dam project when it is listed, the national Bernama news agency reported on Sunday.

Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd is headed for an imminent listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, and Anwar allayed fund managers' fears that the size of the flotation was too large for the public to subscribe.
"I believe there is enough liquidity," Anwar was quoted as saying by Bernama, in response to concern reportedly expressed by some fund managers about the impact of the proposed listing.
Bakun Hydroelectric, constructing a 13.6 billion ($5.45 billion) dam in Malaysia's eastern Sarawak state, has proposed to float a total of 1.5 billion shares of 2.00 ringgit each.
Officials said the listing will be the single largest on the exchange and will raise 3.0 billion ringgit, which will be used almost entirely to fund partial construction of the dam.
The project is led by Ekran Bhd, which has a 32 percent stake in Bakun Hydroelectric.
